chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who gave money to another man to buy a specific type of goods via mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), and he went and bought something other than what he was ordered, he said: 'He is liable (for the difference/value), and the profit is shared between them according to what they stipulated.'

key_terms.الرِّبْحُ: Profit: The gain generated from the trade, shared according to agreement.
key_terms.الْمَتَاعِ: Goods/Merchandise: The items purchased for trade.
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: Liable/Guarantor: Responsible for the value or risk in the transaction.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah: A profit-sharing partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.

ai.seo_question: What happens to profit and liability if an agent buys different goods than specified in a mudarabah contract?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that deviation in the specific commodity purchased during a mudarabah does not invalidate the profit-sharing agreement, provided the agent remains liable for the capital. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence, prioritizing the preservation of the contractual intent over strict adherence to the object of investment. It highlights the principle that the agent's guarantee (daman) ensures the investor's security even when the agent exercises discretion in the type of goods acquired.
